n: As soon as Solomon finished praying, fire fell from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, and God’s glory filled the house. Heaven’s fire was God’s visible “yes” to the prayer and the temple.

f.w: the fire came down from heaven

n: Once again the priests could not enter because of the overwhelming glory. God’s presence, not human effort, made the house holy.

f.w: the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD's house

n: Seeing the fire and glory, all Israel fell face down on the stone pavement and worshipped, repeating the same refrain sung at the ark’s arrival: “For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.”

f.w: For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever

n: The king and people respond to God’s glory by offering sacrifices together.
Solomon offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep — a staggering figure that shows the joy and scale of the dedication.

f.g: Hebrew ḥanak — to inaugurate; related to the later Jewish festival name Hanukkah.

n: Priests and Levites served in their places with the instruments David had made, praising God’s enduring love, as trumpets sounded and all Israel stood.

f.w: instruments of musick of the LORD, which David the king had made

n: There were so many offerings that the bronze altar could not hold them all, so Solomon set apart the center of the courtyard as a holy place for additional sacrifices.

f.g: Grain offerings (‘meat’ in the KJV means food in general).

n: Solomon held the festival for seven days with a vast crowd from the far north (the pass of Hamath) to the far south (the brook of Egypt) — the full extent of the promised land.

f.g: Lebo-hamath, the northern border region in Syria.
The Wadi el-Arish, a seasonal stream on the border with Egypt, not the Nile.

n: Fourteen days of celebration: seven for dedicating the altar and seven for the Feast of Tabernacles, ending with a solemn assembly on the eighth day.

f.g: A sacred gathering marking the end of a festival.

n: On the twenty-third day of the month, Solomon sent the people home happy and grateful for all the good God had done for David, Solomon, and Israel.
Solomon successfully completed both the temple and his palace — everything he had set his heart to do.
Later God appeared to Solomon at night, telling him his prayer was heard and the temple accepted as a house of sacrifice.

f.w: the LORD appeared to Solomon by night

n: God picks up the scenarios of Solomon’s prayer — drought, locusts, plague — acknowledging that such trials might come as discipline.

One of the most loved promises in scripture: if God’s covenant people humble themselves, pray, seek His face, and turn from evil, He will hear, forgive, and heal their land. It is the Chronicler’s key verse on repentance.

f.w: which are called by my name
f.g: People who bear God’s name by covenant.

n: God answers Solomon’s exact request: His eyes will be open and His ears attentive to prayers made in this place.
God declares that He has chosen and made holy this house; His name, eyes, and heart will be there continually. The temple is where God’s heart is turned toward His people.

f.w: mine eyes and mine heart shall be there perpetually

n: God now speaks to Solomon personally: walk before Me as David did, and keep My commandments.

f.g: The Chronicler’s ideal of David is his devotion and repentance, not sinlessness.

n: If Solomon obeys, God will secure his throne and keep His covenant with David — a ruler will never be lacking.
But the warning is equally clear: if they turn away and serve other gods, the blessings will be lost. The “ye” widens the warning to all Israel.
Israel would be uprooted from the land and even this glorious temple rejected and mocked by the nations. This happened when Babylon destroyed it in 587 BC.

f.g: An object of ridicule and scorn.

f.w: pluck them up by the roots

n: Passers-by would be shocked to see such a grand temple in ruins and would ask why the Lord allowed it.

f.g: Something that causes horror and amazement.

n: The answer would be plain: because they abandoned the God who freed them from Egypt and served other gods. Sacred buildings are no protection without faithful hearts.

f.w: therefore hath he brought all this evil upon them
